Canary Wharf student complex claims tallest passivhaus title
stories.summary: The urbanest student accommodation cluster in Canary Wharf has reached 46 storeys, earning the title of the world's tallest passivhaus building. Designed by Apt Architects, the project provides 1,672 beds for University College London students. The certification confirms the building is also the world's largest residential passivhaus project.

stories.summary: Certifier Laszlo Lepp of the Passivhaus Institute handed over the paperwork on November 24 that makes a 136.8-metre student complex in Canary Wharf the tallest Passivhaus building in the world, with 1,672 beds for University College London students. The scheme is urbanest Canary Wharf, three towers of 46, 36 and

stories.title: India’s green and net-zero building movement gets CII-IGBC push - Construction Week India
Maharashtra leads India in green building projects
stories.summary: Maharashtra has reached 4,754 green building projects covering 5.01 billion square feet. The state government encourages this growth by offering additional floor area ratio incentives of 3% to 7% for projects achieving IGBC Silver, Gold, or Platinum certification. The state aims to accelerate the transition to net-zero.

stories.title: DS Group's Renaissance Bengaluru Race Course Hotel Achieves LEED Platinum Certification - India Education Diary
ACE Powerhouse wins second consecutive green building award
stories.summary: The ACE Powerhouse at Campus Skellefteå has won the 2026 MB Plus Project of the Year award at the Sweden Green Building Awards. This follows its recognition as Environmental Building of the Year in 2025. The project is cited as proof of long-term sustainability and innovative collaboration.

stories.title: IGBC and CAHO partner for sustainable healthcare
stories.summary: The Indian Green Building Council and the Consortium of Accredited Healthcare Organisations have signed a memorandum of understanding to promote resource-efficient and climate-resilient healthcare infrastructure. The partnership aims to integrate green principles into the national healthcare sector through institutional collaboration between the two organizations.

stories.title: Indian Green Building Council To Make Sustainable Structures In Bhutan - NDTV
Kembhavi Architecture Foundation designs new university headquarters
stories.summary: Architect Soumya Shetty Kembhavi has completed the design for the Karnataka State Law University administration building in Hubballi. Commissioned by the state government, the facility provides a dedicated headquarters for the university. The design features a wide entrance staircase leading to a main pavilion and administrative offices.

stories.title: Emaar India announces new office tower in Gurugram
stories.summary: Emaar India is developing Emaar Business Square, a Grade-A commercial tower in Sector 65, Gurugram. The project is pre-certified IGBC Platinum and includes ground-floor retail space. Located near major roads, the developer claims the site offers occupiers access to talent and the potential for shorter employee commutes.

stories.title: Gurugram office market sees rising rents and absorption
stories.summary: Emaar India is developing a new office tower in Gurugram as the region reports 3.8 million square feet of leasing in the third quarter of 2026. Grade A office rents in the city rose 12% to 15% year on year, with vacancy rates falling to 17.6%.

stories.title: Take a look inside AARQE9’s Golf Links Project in New Delhi where maximalism meets personal expression - Architect and I
Look inside a contemporary house rooted in the traditions of Kerala - Architect and Interiors India
Take a tour inside the 2500 sq ft Mumbai residence that finds its character in simplicity - Architect and Interiors Indi
Take a tour inside 18000 sq ft TruNativ’s Mumbai office that reimagines the language of corporate interiors - Architect
Designer uses raw finishes for Rajkot family home
stories.summary: Ayushi Shah of Shisht Design Studio has completed an 1,800-square-foot home in Rajkot using raw material finishes and color. The project was designed to balance everyday functionality with a space for family memories across three generations. The designer focused on the expressive nature of honest building materials.

stories.title: Harisadan by Uncut Design Lab: Reworking a rest house in Tirumala - Hotelier India
AJ Architecture Awards 2026 winners announced
stories.summary: The annual awards recognized 21 projects from a 123-project shortlist, ranging from a 3.4km-long viaduct to a small studio for an international DJ. A panel of 64 expert judges traveled across the country to visit every scheme. The awards celebrate outstanding built architecture across the UK.

stories.title: Tuckey Design Studio’s Rammed Earth House wins Manser Medal
stories.summary: The winning house features rammed earth walls made from excavated clay, demolition aggregate, and limestone gravel. The project contains no cement stabilizer and uses reclaimed timber from a dockyard. Judges described the house as carved from the earth, noting it seems crafted rather than built.

stories.title: V&A East Storehouse named AJ Design of the Year
stories.summary: The 16,000m² facility houses over 250,000 items from the V&A collections. The AJ editorial team described the project as both functional and wonderful. It is the first open-access museum storehouse of its kind, occupying a former London Olympics media center reworked by Hawkins\Brown.

stories.title: IFDO named AJ Architect of the Year 2026
stories.summary: The practice won the title as two of its three founders prepare to leave the firm. Thomas Bryans will take full ownership of the 15-strong practice. The award follows the firm's success at the AJ Retrofit & Reuse Awards for its work on a historic building in Hastings.

stories.title: Metropolitan Workshop’s Farmstead Road is Editor’s Choice
stories.summary: The scheme replaced a two-storey terrace with 24 affordable homes on a modest site in Lewisham. Designed to Passivhaus standards, the project provides two- and three-bedroom housing. The AJ editorial team praised the collaboration between an ambitious client and an equally ambitious architect.

stories.title: Doolan Prize 2026: Scotland’s best building announced
stories.summary: Bennetts Associates won for the retrofit of a Category A-listed Victorian hospital, which had been empty since 2003. The project created a 450-seat auditorium and teaching spaces for the University of Edinburgh. The scheme saved the former NHS building from falling into total dereliction.

stories.title: World Architecture Festival names academic building as top project
stories.summary: Prestige University’s new academic building in India won World Building of the Year. The structure features a 9,000-seat open-air amphitheater roof composed of 463 stepped platforms. Architects drew inspiration from ancient Indian stepwells, which have served local communities for over a millennium.

stories.title: Studio Gang completes Women’s Leadership Center
stories.summary: The 24,000-square-foot campus in Wisconsin was designed for women leaders to gather and work. Founder Ann Drake noted that women often spend their careers in rooms never designed with them in mind. Studio Gang responded with architecture intended to address that specific oversight.

stories.title: Europe’s largest museum development opens in Brussels
stories.summary: The former Citroën garage has been transformed into Kanal, a 40,000-square-metre museum for modern art and architecture. The project, which includes an exhibition programme developed with the Centre Pompidou, claims to be Europe’s largest museum development. It occupies a restored 1930s industrial building.

stories.title: National Grid tests 3D-printed foundations
stories.summary: The UK has struggled with infrastructure delivery, as 58% of recent road projects were delivered late. National Grid is now testing 3D-printed foundations at its substations. The move follows research showing that large projects are frequently waylaid by factors including the Great British weather.

stories.title: Fabri uses 3D printed patterns for metal casting
stories.summary: The foundry has replaced traditional steel tooling and wax patterns with 3D printed resin patterns and proprietary software. Co-founder Steven Davis claims the company can move from design to a finished part in one week. The firm produces components for munitions, aviation, and naval applications.

stories.title: Titomic USA secures $250 million defense subcontract
stories.summary: The subsidiary of Titomic Limited received a sole-source framework agreement running through December 2031. The contract covers hypersonics, missile, and aerospace work. The company uses its patented kinetic fusion cold spray process for industrial-scale metal additive manufacturing, coating, and repair.

stories.title: Domin expands 3D printed hydraulics production to U.S.
stories.summary: The UK manufacturer is investing $16.2 million to build its first North American site in North Carolina. The project is expected to create 204 jobs. The company combines 3D metal printing with digital control to produce valves and actuators marketed as smaller and lighter than conventional parts.

stories.title: Arkema honored for bio-based material innovations
stories.summary: Arkema won an innovation award for low-density polyamide 11 and a high-performance instant adhesive with 60% bio-based content. The company transforms drought-resistant castor beans into specialty materials. The award recognizes innovations that have successfully reached the market and delivered measurable business and sustainability results.

stories.title: Siemens digital twin targets 20% cut in hydrogen costs
stories.summary: Siemens is developing a digital twin for green hydrogen production and renewable-powered AI computing. The project aims to reduce production costs by up to 20% while accelerating gigawatt-scale energy infrastructure. It highlights the growing role of simulation in addressing the energy demands of AI.

stories.title: Architectural metalwork market shifts toward green retrofits
stories.summary: The global market for architectural metalwork enters 2026 shaped by decarbonization mandates and the industrialization of construction. The sector, which includes curtain wall systems and structural framing, is increasingly specified for green retrofits and prefabricated façades as procurement behavior becomes more disciplined.

stories.title: Recycled plastics market moves into construction mainstream
stories.summary: The global market for recycled plastics in green building is transitioning from a sustainability niche to a mainstream construction segment. The product scope includes HDPE, PET, and PVC processed into decking, insulation, and modular components. Adoption is driven by circular construction mandates.

stories.title: Research examines bamboo fibre for road construction
stories.summary: Engineers presented research on using waste bamboo fibre in bituminous road construction at the Indian Roads Congress. The study investigated whether the waste material could be converted into an input for high-quality dense bituminous macadam. Experts gathered in Hyderabad to discuss sustainable road structures.

stories.title: Designing for the Cold: How Kashmir’s Homes Beat Harsh Winters - Realty Plus Magazine
Net-Zero Buildings: Design Principles for a Low-Carbon Future - Realty Plus Magazine
Indian cities show seasonal heat shifts
stories.summary: Researchers found that Indian urban heat islands shift seasonally, with rural agricultural lands becoming hotter than city cores during dry summers. Cities then emerge as heat islands during monsoon and winter periods. The study evaluates research from 1990 to 2023 to compare Indian findings against global trends.

stories.title: Pune heat maps reveal industrial source
stories.summary: A study using satellite data found that Pune's hottest areas form a connected network rather than isolated patches. The Pimpri Chinchwad industrial belt emerged as the primary source of the city's heat. Surface temperatures in the region reached 75.4 degrees Celsius, according to the researchers.

stories.title: Students develop biological building cooling
stories.summary: Students from MIT World Peace University developed a biological coating using algae, moss and cyanobacteria to cool building exteriors. The project aims to reduce dependence on conventional cooling systems and was recently recognized at the 8th International Conference on Sustainability Education in New Delhi.

stories.title: Pollution control remains a seasonal effort
stories.summary: Air pollution in Indian cities is a year-round crisis that currently receives administrative attention primarily during winter months. Experts argue that seasonal restrictions on construction and vehicles are insufficient to address the deeper, persistent problems of urban planning, emissions and governance that remain throughout the year.

stories.title: Bangladesh looks to climate-responsive architecture
stories.summary: The 2026 UN Climate Change Conference has prompted calls for Bangladesh to rethink its construction industry and prioritize climate-responsive design. Rising sea levels, cyclones and heatwaves are transforming the country's built environment, making sustainable development a central challenge for national infrastructure and public health.

stories.title: Can Roof Tiles Reduce Indoor Heat? India Is Finding Out. - The New York Times
Policy tool could certify chemical-free farms
stories.summary: India's Large Area Conversion policy allows the government to certify entire regions as chemical-free without requiring individual audits or transition periods. The policy is suggested as a way to recognize traditional farming practices in heritage sites like Koraput, Odisha, without imposing significant costs on local farmers.

stories.title: Sinking African cities face flood risk
stories.summary: New research suggests sinking land and rising seas could expose seven million people in African coastal megacities to flooding by 2050. Under moderate warming, an extreme sea level event could threaten one million buildings and 180 billion dollars in assets across 20 populous coastal cities.

stories.title: Hyderabad road width limits mobility
stories.summary: Nearly 90 percent of Hyderabad's road network consists of roads less than 10 metres wide. WRI India CEO Madhav Pai stated that this planning gap hinders the city's ability to accommodate growing traffic and future infrastructure needs, requiring systematic land aggregation and redevelopment of existing networks.

stories.title: Maharashtra urged to unify transport authority
stories.summary: Transport experts are calling for the state government to fast-track legislation for a Unified Metropolitan Transport Authority in Pune. The current coordination mechanism lacks the power to ensure agencies act on decisions, leaving commuters to navigate gaps in last-mile connectivity and Metro station access.

stories.title: Gurugram to convert parks into ponds
stories.summary: Gurugram plans to develop water retention ponds across 247 acres of parks to curb recurring waterlogging. The move follows 300 crore rupees in drainage spending over three years that failed to resolve the issue. The ponds are intended to hold rainwater before it reaches residential areas.

stories.title: Guwahati drains clogged by litter
stories.summary: Urban flooding concerns in Guwahati have intensified as litter continues to choke the city's drainage infrastructure. The accumulation of waste in drains remains a primary factor in the city's inability to manage heavy rainfall, leading to recurring waterlogging in urban areas.

stories.title: Thiruvananthapuram mayor blames rain intensity
stories.summary: Thiruvananthapuram mayor V V Rajesh attributed recent widespread waterlogging to unusually heavy rainfall, noting that a day's worth of rain fell within an hour. The city corporation and opposition parties traded charges over drainage preparedness after the showers disrupted traffic and flooded the city centre.

stories.title: Liveability requires focus on public spaces
stories.summary: Architect Dikshu Kukreja argues that India's rapid urbanization is placing unsustainable pressure on metropolitan infrastructure and social equity. He suggests that tier-II and tier-III cities must be developed as viable alternatives to major metros, emphasizing that public spaces are as critical as buildings for city liveability.

stories.title: Urban growth shifts to census towns
stories.summary: Dr. Debolina Kundu of the National Institute of Urban Affairs notes that India's urban expansion is increasingly driven by the transformation of rural settlements into census towns. Satellite data shows outward expansion of built-up areas is a significant factor in urbanization, outpacing migration-led growth in many regions.

stories.title: Planning gaps persist in Indian cities
stories.summary: Sunita Kohli argues that India's development process has historically prioritized engineering and architecture over comprehensive urban planning. She cites Gurugram as an example of how inadequate planning affects both residential and commercial environments, calling for more inclusive and liveable urban development across all city tiers.

stories.title: Synaps 2.0 and the search for architectural efficiency
stories.summary: Architecture remains a field defined by the translation of abstract concepts into technical documents. Despite decades of computer-aided design, the industry maintains that this translation process is one of its most time-consuming aspects. Technology continues to promise a faster path from imagination to construction.

stories.title: Pulley raises $41M Series B to speed up construction permitting - Dealroom
Programa adds SketchUp extension to reduce data entry
stories.summary: Studio operations software Programa has launched a SketchUp extension designed to connect 3D models with its product schedules. The company claims the tool frees designers from duplicating information. It replaces spreadsheets by linking model components directly to item codes, supplier details, dimensions, and pricing.

stories.title: Gstarsoft promotes CAD to BIM transition at Munich event
stories.summary: Gstarsoft is using BIM World Munich 2026 to demonstrate how teams can adopt building information modelling while retaining their existing CAD practices. The company is showcasing AI-assisted design visualisation and cloud-based drawing reviews. The path to the future involves keeping the tools of the past.

stories.title: Federico II University wins digital management award
stories.summary: The University of Naples Federico II has won the 2026 BIM&Digital Award for its project, From Maintenance to Digital Heritage. The initiative focuses on digitising the maintenance management of the university’s real estate portfolio. The project aims to turn physical assets into digital data.

stories.title: Univers expands Physical AI ecosystem with new partnerships
stories.summary: Univers has announced three global partnerships to apply Physical AI across the built environment, maritime, and industrial sectors. The company, which describes itself as a global leader in intelligent infrastructure, aims to make critical systems intelligent. The ecosystem is growing, according to the company.

stories.title: Construction industry sees rise in vision-language models
stories.summary: The Korea Information Service of the Construction Industry reports that AI systems connecting perception, judgment, and action are reaching maturity. A prominent development includes vision-language models used for safety management. The industry is now evaluating contextual information through a two-stage cascade architecture.

stories.title: Mouse Computer to showcase verified PCs for construction
stories.summary: Mouse Computer will exhibit at the 6th Construction DX Exhibition in Tokyo this December. The company plans to showcase hardware verified for use with Vectorworks and TREND-POINT software. Visitors can experience the processing performance required for construction and civil engineering tasks at the booth.

stories.title: South Korean construction expo highlights safety tech
stories.summary: The 2026 Smart Construction Safety & AI Expo revealed current industry priorities in South Korea. Participants focused on vision-language model-based false alarm filtering and real-time safety management solutions. The sector is currently managing the transition toward automated safety monitoring systems.

stories.title: Navrachana University hosts Asian Congress of Semiotics
stories.summary: Navrachana University has inaugurated the third Asian Congress of Semiotics, marking the conference's first time in India. The event focuses on how meanings are created through social, visual, and technological practices. The university received 93 abstracts for the gathering.

stories.title: CIMP and Kyonggi University partner on AI research
stories.summary: Chandragupt Institute of Management Patna and South Korea’s Kyonggi University have signed an agreement to apply artificial intelligence to agriculture, urban planning, and tourism in Bihar. The two institutions plan to pursue joint research and faculty exchanges under the Korea-Bihar AI Future Generation Programme.

stories.title: Mumbai University and IGBC launch green building course
stories.summary: The Indian Green Building Council and the University of Mumbai have signed an agreement to develop a specialised course on the green built environment. The partnership aims to create a talent pool for India’s sustainable construction sector by training students in civil, electrical, and mechanical engineering.

stories.title: IGBC and Mumbai University partner for green education
stories.summary: The Indian Green Building Council and the University of Mumbai have partnered to develop a curriculum focused on the green built environment. The initiative targets students in engineering and architecture to prepare them for the sustainable construction sector. Education is being aligned with industry standards.

stories.title: CII IGBC and University of Mumbai sign MoU to strengthen green education and develop industry-ready talent for sustainab
Drury architecture students build greenhouses for residents
stories.summary: Architecture students at Drury University are constructing greenhouses for residents of Eden Village 2. The project follows the personal recovery journey of a resident who found stability through gardening. The students are applying their design skills to support the community's existing living space.

stories.title: UBC Applied Science graduates present research
stories.summary: Four graduates from UBC Applied Science have presented research on topics ranging from food inflation to cardiac care access. The students turned their academic inquiries into real-world designs and policy recommendations. The university continues to frame research as a tool for societal change.

stories.title: SRM University opens B.Arch admission process
stories.summary: SRM University has released information regarding its 2027 B.Arch admission cycle. The institution is providing details on eligibility criteria and application procedures for prospective architecture students.

stories.title: CEPT University president discusses AI in architecture
stories.summary: Prof Barjor Mehta of CEPT University says higher education must bridge the gap between academic learning and professional practice. He advocates for studio-based learning and the integration of artificial intelligence into architecture and planning. The goal is to prepare students for real-world urban challenges.

research.summary: The deep sea has long been considered a safe haven for marine life, but new genetic research suggests a hidden biodiversity crisis may be unfolding far beneath the waves. Scientists analyzing more than a decade of genetic data from five species of deep-sea fish and shrimp in the.

research.title: Scientists turn one of the world’s hardest-to-recycle plastics into high-performance lubricating oil
research.summary: Virginia Tech scientists have discovered how to transform one of the world's hardest-to-recycle plastics into a valuable ingredient for high-performance engine oil. Their innovative process converts discarded PVC into a useful lubricant material in just three hours. The breakthrough could turn a major source of plastic pollution into.

research.title: Earth's core may be leaking a 4.5-billion-year-old secret
research.summary: Scientists have discovered an unusual carbon signature in Hawaiian volcanic rocks that suggests some of Earth's carbon originated in ancient meteorites and later escaped from deep within the planet's core. The discovery raises an astonishing possibility: Carbon essential to life may have traveled from space to Earth's depths.
